note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Prepare statements run in one PowerShell session with the episode folder as current directory; variables do not survive into the screens, so each screen re-derives what it needs.
prepare: # owner, once: VS Code with C# Dev Kit (check the licence first) and REST Client, Docker Desktop, .NET SDK 10
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\work | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-debug, C:\work\orders-history -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
dotnet tool restore; dotnet build src/Contoso.Orders.Api; dotnet test
git init -q -b main; git config core.autocrlf false; git config user.name 'Alex Demo'; git config user.email 'alex.demo@contoso.com'
git add -A; git commit -q -m "feat(reports): monthly revenue per customer"

screens.name: redtest
screens.app: VS Code (C# Dev Kit, Testing view)
steps: Open C:\work\orders-debug in VS Code; Source Control shows the 5-line change in Reports.cs (patch 01 applied by prepare)
Testing view: run MonthEnd_orders_are_part_of_the_month and Every_order_lands_in_exactly_one_month
Capture both red, the message 'Expected: 30' / 'Actual: 29' (and 237 / 230) and the failing line highlighted in the editor
mask: Windows user name in the title bar, paths and recent list (folder is under C:\work)
screens.note: C# Dev Kit needs a Visual Studio Professional/Enterprise subscription for organisations (Learn, Eligibility). If there is none, use the open-source C# extension and show dotnet test output instead.

screens.name: debugger
steps: Run and Debug view > 'Orders API (debug)' > F5 (runs the build task first; the API listens on http://localhost:8080; stop the Docker container first)
Set a breakpoint on the 'var customers = ...' line of Reports.MonthlyRevenueAsync (the first line after ToListAsync)
Open .vscode/orders.http and click Send Request on GET /reports/monthly?month=2026-01
Stopped: Variables (firstDay and lastDay), Watch orders.Count = 29; Debug Console: orders.Any(o => o.Created == new DateOnly(2026, 1, 31)) -> false; hover an Order for the DebuggerDisplay text

Right-click the gutter at the 'return new MonthlyRevenue(...)' line > Add Logpoint with {firstDay} has {orders.Count} orders; right-click the first breakpoint > Edit Breakpoint > Expression: firstDay.Month == 1
Send the January request again, then month=2026-03: the breakpoint stops only for January and the logpoint prints in the Debug Console without stopping
Stop the session, revert the bug (git apply -R bugs\01-month-end-off-by-one.patch), run the two tests: green; commit 'fix(reports): a month is a half-open range'
mask: Windows user name in the title bar, paths and recent list (folder is under C:\work)

screens.name: trace
prepare: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='dotnet.exe'" | Where-Object CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api.dll*' | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }
screens.note: Runs in PowerShell 7 (no BOM problem). Expect HTTP/1.1 400, the traceId field, one 'Warning Contoso.Orders.Reports: Rejected month 2026-13: expected yyyy-MM' line and the raw JSON line with its Scopes array and TraceId 4bf92f35...

screens.name: hang
prepare: if (Get-Command docker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { docker rm -f orders-api 2>$null }
commands: dotnet tool run dotnet-stack ps | Select-String Contoso.Orders.Api
# the dump holds the whole heap: delete it
screens.note: Windows is new here: dotnet-dump collect writes a Windows dump, syncblk and clrstack -all should read the same. If a step fails in Git Bash, run the script's commands by hand and fix scripts/triage-hang.sh (report it). A heap dump of this API was 232 MB on Linux: check free disk space.

teardown: docker rm -f orders-api 2>$null; docker rmi contoso/orders-api:dev
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='dotnet.exe'" | Where-Object CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api.dll*' | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }
# owner: VS Code > Run > Remove All Breakpoints (extensions stay)
Set-Location C:\work; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-debug, C:\work\orders-history -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
prepare_local: Use-DotNetSdk -Channel 10.0   # kit helper: uses the installed .NET 10 SDK, else installs it into C:\MGLab\dotnet (no admin)

Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'Contoso.Orders.Api.exe' -or ($_.Name -eq 'dotnet.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api*') } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }   # no orders API left running (it would lock bin)
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\work | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-debug -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
dotnet tool restore; dotnet build src/Contoso.Orders.Api -v q --nologo; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'dotnet build failed' }
git init -q -b main; git config core.autocrlf false; git config user.name 'Alex Demo'; git config user.email 'alex.demo@contoso.com'
git add -A; git commit -q -m "feat(reports): monthly revenue per customer"
teardown_local: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'Contoso.Orders.Api.exe' -or ($_.Name -eq 'dotnet.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api*') } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }   # no orders API left running (it would lock bin)
